sec: Uric acid nephropathy (tumour lysis syndrome) · p801

items.q: Uric acid nephropathy is also known as:
items.exp: Uric acid nephropathy AKA tumour lysis syndrome — a renal cause of AKI. (Book p801)

opts: Hematological malignancies within a few days of the onset of treatment
Solid tumours several years after chemotherapy
Chronic kidney disease after contrast exposure
items.exp: Cause: hematological malignancies within a few days of onset of Rx (chemotherapy). (Book p801)

items.q: Complete the pathophysiology flowchart of uric acid nephropathy — 1) Leukemia/lymphoma  2) Tumour cells  3) Effect … A) Rapid multiplication  B) ↑Uric acid filtered by the glomerulus  C) Underlying malignancy
items.exp: Flowchart: leukemia/lymphoma → rapid multiplication of tumour cells → ↑uric acid filtered by the glomerulus. (Book p801)

items.q: Match the features of uric acid nephropathy — 1) Renal presentation  2) Serum uric acid  3) Other electrolytes  4) Serum calcium … A) ↑  B) Oliguric AKI  C) S.K⁺/S.PO₄³⁻/S.mg²⁺ ↑  D) ↓S.Ca²⁺
items.exp: Features of uric acid nephropathy: oliguric AKI; S. uric acid ↑↑; S. K⁺/S. PO₄³⁻/S. mg²⁺ ↑; ↓S. Ca²⁺. (Book p801)

items.q: A 24-year-old with Burkitt lymphoma develops oliguric AKI 3 days after starting chemotherapy, with a uric acid of 14 mg/dL, K⁺ 6.2, PO₄³⁻ 7 mg/dL and Ca²⁺ 7.4 mg/dL. The diagnosis is:
items.exp: Uric acid nephropathy (TLS): oliguric AKI with ↑↑uric acid, ↑K⁺/PO₄³⁻/mg²⁺ and ↓Ca²⁺, occurring within days of starting treatment of a haematological malignancy. (Book p801)

items.q: Hypocalcemia is a described feature of uric acid nephropathy.
opts: False — calcium always rises in tumour lysis syndrome
False — calcium is normal in uric acid nephropathy
items.exp: Features: oliguric AKI, S. uric acid ↑↑, ↑S.K⁺/S.PO₄³⁻/S.mg²⁺ and ↓S.Ca²⁺. (Book p801)

items.q: The serum potassium, phosphate and magnesium changes in uric acid nephropathy are:
opts: Potassium raised with phosphate and magnesium reduced
items.exp: In uric acid nephropathy, S. K⁺, S. PO₄³⁻ and S. mg²⁺ all rise (↑) while serum calcium falls. (Book p801)

items.q: All but one of the following are features of uric acid nephropathy. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Uric acid nephropathy: oliguric AKI with ↑↑uric acid, ↑K⁺/PO₄/mg²⁺ and ↓Ca²⁺ — calcium falls, so hypercalcemia is not a feature. (Book p801)
